name: residual_dividend_signed_surplus
question_template: Use exact arithmetic. A firm follows a strict residual dividend policy. Next year's capital budget is {CAPEX} USD million and the target equity ratio is {EQUITY_RATIO} percent of the capital budget, so the equity required equals the capital budget times that ratio. Base net income is {NET_INCOME} USD million, and a one-time after-tax item changes it by {ADJ} percent of base net income (a negative value is a loss, a positive value is a gain), giving adjusted net income. The signed surplus equals adjusted net income minus the equity required; a negative surplus means a shortfall. Any positive surplus is paid out entirely as dividends. If the surplus is negative, the firm issues new equity for the full shortfall and pays a zero dividend. Report the total dividend paid in USD million.

slots.description: Equity portion of the capital budget at the target equity ratio
Net income after the signed one-time after-tax item
Adjusted net income minus equity required; negative means shortfall
New equity raised to cover any shortfall; zero if no shortfall

program:
def solve():
    capex = Q(P["CAPEX"])
    er = Q(P["EQUITY_RATIO"]) / 100
    ni = Q(P["NET_INCOME"])
    adj = Q(P["ADJ"]) / 100
    equity_required = capex * er
    adjusted_ni = ni * (1 + adj)
    surplus = adjusted_ni - equity_required
    if surplus >= 0:
        dividend = surplus
        issued = Q(0)
    else:
        dividend = Q(0)
        issued = -surplus
    return {
        "final": dividend,
        "equity_required": equity_required,
        "adjusted_net_income": adjusted_ni,
        "signed_surplus": surplus,
        "equity_issued": issued,
    }
